findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of M2-S41-T2, which is also set in CI pull request reviews with too many false positives. It pits a confidence or conservatism instruction against explicit report-and-skip categories, and the categories win. Asking the reader to predict the result of a test on 200 labeled pull requests rather than to pick the fix changes only the framing. The same reasoning leads to the answer: confidence-based instructions do not raise precision, while categorical criteria do. M4-S09-T2 already covers why the high-confidence instruction fails.

blind_answer.reason: Per 4.1-K2/S1, generic confidence instructions fail to improve precision compared to specific categorical report/skip criteria; the confidence line mainly reduces volume without raising the valid-finding share much.
